The Moon Mars Deep Space Sources
Research file 01

The Moon: A Museum Without Walls

The Apollo missions left behind more than footprints. Astronauts deployed scientific instruments, tools and equipment to help scientists study the Moon. Some hardware remained on the lunar surface after the astronauts returned to Earth.

Scientific instrument

Apollo 11 Seismometer

21 days

The first seismometer placed on the Moon recorded moonquakes and meteorite impacts. Its data gave scientists an early look at the Moon's internal structure.

Long-running research

Apollo Lunar Experiments

Until 1977

More advanced experiment stations were deployed on later Apollo missions. Instruments at five lunar stations sent scientific data to Earth until NASA ended the program in September 1977.

Why was the equipment left there?

Returning every instrument to Earth would have required extra space, fuel and time. Many experiments were designed to stay on the Moon and send their results back by radio.

What did scientists learn?

The instruments helped researchers study moonquakes, meteorite impacts, heat flow and the Moon's internal structure. Their measurements expanded our knowledge long after the astronauts had left.

Research note: NASA reports that the Apollo 11 seismometer returned data for about three weeks. Later Apollo experiment stations continued transmitting until September 1977.

Research file 02

Mars: Robots That Outlived Their Missions

Mars rovers are robotic vehicles that explore the planet's surface. They take photographs, study rocks and soil, and send information back to Earth. Several rovers continued working far beyond their original mission plans.

How Far Have the Rovers Travelled?

Spirit

45.16 km

45.22 km

Data snapshot: NASA's rover-distance update dated October 11, 2026. Perseverance's distance is still increasing, so this is not its final total.

2004–2011

Spirit

Spirit was designed for a 90-Martian-day mission but operated for more than six years. It found evidence that ancient Mars was much wetter than it is today and travelled about 7.7 kilometres.

2004–2018

Opportunity

Opportunity operated for almost 15 years. It found evidence that ancient Mars may once have had conditions that could support microbial life and travelled more than 45 kilometres.

2012–present

Curiosity

Curiosity studies rocks and the ancient environments of Gale Crater. Its instruments found chemical and mineral evidence that Mars once had environments that could support microbial life.

2021–present

Perseverance

Perseverance explores Jezero Crater, an area that once contained a river delta. It searches for signs of ancient microbial life and collects rock samples for possible future return to Earth.

Why are rovers important?

Rovers can travel across the surface and examine places that are difficult for humans to reach. They help scientists study the planet's geology, climate and past water activity.

Why do some rovers stop working?

Dust, extreme temperatures, worn parts and limited power can affect a rover. Even after a rover stops communicating, the information it collected can remain useful to scientists.

Research file 03

Deep Space: Messages Beyond the Planets

Some spacecraft do not land on a planet. Instead, they fly past distant worlds, study their environments and continue travelling through space. The Voyager spacecraft are famous examples of long-lasting robotic explorers.

Launched 1977

Voyager 1

Voyager 1 flew past Jupiter and Saturn. It entered interstellar space in August 2012 and is the most distant human-made object.

Launched 1977

Voyager 2

Voyager 2 explored Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune. It entered interstellar space in November 2018.

1977 – The journey beginsVoyager 1 and Voyager 2 launch from Earth to explore the outer planets.
1979 – JupiterThe spacecraft send back close-up observations of Jupiter and its moons.
1980–1989 – The outer planetsVoyager 1 studies Saturn. Voyager 2 continues on to Uranus and Neptune.
2012 – Voyager 1Voyager 1 crosses into interstellar space.
2018 – Voyager 2Voyager 2 also crosses into interstellar space.

What is the Golden Record?

Each Voyager spacecraft carries a gold-plated record containing sounds and images selected to represent life and culture on Earth. It is a message from humanity, designed to travel far beyond our planet.

Why are the Voyagers special?

They show how spacecraft can continue exploring long after their original planetary flyby missions. Their data helps scientists study regions of space far beyond the planets.

The people behind the project

Curiosity brought us here.

We are a team of students from KBTC International School, exploring the stories and histories behind the machines that had once helped humanity reach farther into the ever-unknown space.

Our team

TRIALS AND ERRORS

Learning through curiosity, teamwork and every failed attempt. We believe that every discovery always starts with a question and every mistake is always chance to learn. As said, take chances, make mistakes.

Our mission

Remember the machines. Share the science.

Our goal is to make space exploration engaging and understandable for school-age students by telling the stories of NASA's space hardware, its missions and its scientific contributions.
